# `columnConfigs`: one record per column

Part of [generated data](../generated-data.md). `emptyValueAllowed` is declared, `isFormula` is sampled, and `valueName` is declared first and sampled only as a fallback, with a summary of the columns it had to guess.

## What is generated per column

**`columnConfigs`** (`generated/columnConfigs.ts`) — generated by `ColumnConfigOperator` (`05_Operators`) from the "Column Config" sheet. No longer stores a column's index (`colIndex`) — `03_SpreadsheetIdentified` resolves that live from `columnId` instead, since a stored index would go stale as columns are added/removed/reordered. Per column, `columnId`/`valueName`/`header`/`isFormula`/`emptyValueAllowed` are generated; `customDefaultValue` is always emitted at its default for now.

## `emptyValueAllowed` is declared

**`emptyValueAllowed` is *declared*** — read straight off the column's own box in Column Config (#13), which the correction pass never rewrites except on a **self-describing row**, so a tick survives a sync on a business column. A column nobody has ticked emits `false`, which is what every column emitted before, so ticking is opt-in one column at a time; don't bulk-tick formula columns, since a formula that yields a blank under some conditions and a value under others is exactly the case worth declaring individually. A newly discovered column arrives unticked, so nothing starts accepting blanks on the operator's behalf.

## `isFormula` is sampled

**`isFormula` is *sampled* — read off the described column's top data-row cell at emit time (`activeIsFormula`), not declared, and not stored on Column Config** — so it can flip between regenerations if someone edits that cell. Fine as data; treat it with care as a *type* axis, since a routine `gen:configs` run can then change which columns satisfy a constraint, and the resulting error surfaces far from the spreadsheet edit that caused it.

## A boolean trait keeps its literal type

A boolean trait in the generated data does keep its literal type per column, because `boolean` is a union of literal types and contextual typing doesn't widen it — that's what lets `ColumnIsFormula` resolve to `true` or `false` rather than `boolean`, and it holds for any boolean trait the config gains later.

## `customDefaultValue` is reserved, not implemented

`customDefaultValue` is meant to override what a column writes when something fills it with a default, the way `updateToDefault` and the default-append path do, but it isn't implemented and may be dropped if no use case turns up — don't repurpose it for something else in the meantime (a read-time coercion, say, belongs on the value schema rather than on a per-column trait; #12).

## How `valueName` is resolved

**`valueName` is declared-first, sampled only as a fallback.**

The sync resolves it in six steps, first match winning: the ID column is always `id`; then a `=valueConfig[...]` data-validation rule names its value; then the column's own **declared column type** — the one an operator picks in the Sheets column-type menu, delivered as `columnType` on the table's `columnProperties` — maps to a primitive (`DOUBLE`/`CURRENCY`/`PERCENT` → number, `DATE` → date, `TIME`/`DATE_TIME` → **number**, `TEXT` and the chip types → string, `BOOLEAN` → **checkbox**; `DROPDOWN` and `COLUMN_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED` map to nothing and fall through); then **BOOLEAN data validation** (Insert > Checkbox) on the Table column, or on the first data row if the Table did not name BOOLEAN, declares **checkbox** (`condition.type === BOOLEAN`, no values list required; other condition types are ignored here); then a **compatible number format** on the first data row maps to a primitive (`NUMBER`/`CURRENCY`/`PERCENT`/`SCIENTIFIC`/`TIME`/`DATE_TIME` → number, `DATE` → date, `TEXT` → string; omitted or `NUMBER_FORMAT_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED` map to nothing). Compatible means the name the sample would guess from that row equals the format's mapped name; a blank counts because that guess already consults the format. An incompatible sample stays a guess and stays untyped.

## `checkbox` comes only from a declaration

**`checkbox` is produced by declaration and by nothing else** (#12, #42) — the type menu or BOOLEAN validation, never the sample: a column that merely holds `TRUE` still produces `boolean` and stays untyped. Declaring checkbox is what buys the never-blank guarantee, so a column that samples as boolean satisfies neither the selector nor the checkbox operator, and the fix is to declare it in Sheets rather than to widen the filter. Only when nothing declares it does the old top-data-row sample decide. Every one of a checkbox column's rows draws a box, so a row nobody has touched counts as unchecked rather than as blank.

## A compatible number format is a declaration

**A compatible number format is a declaration, not a guess** (#42), including a blank first data row that inherited Currency — the type menu is never rewritten. Measured on Occupancy, 10 September 2026: "Next terms notes" was blank, undeclared and `CURRENCY`-formatted, and generated as a number; that column is now declared number and leaves the untyped list. A notes column that already contains text stays guessed string and untyped.

## Only a whole-day column is a `date`

**Only a whole-day column is a `date`** (#15) — a value name whose type is `SerialDate`, which a time-of-day serial would not satisfy, so the datetime formats map to plain numbers until there is a datetime value name to give them.

## The untyped-columns summary

Because a column left on Automatic with no mapped format and no Insert > Checkbox declares nothing, the sample is still doing real work: **the sync counts every column whose value name it had to guess and returns a one-line summary**, which the config-sync endpoint writes into its run status cell; the per-sheet breakdown goes to the execution log. The sync never fails over an untyped column — it also writes missing column IDs and appends Column Config rows, and a throw would discard all of that. **That run status cell is written by the endpoint, not by the sync.** `npm run gen:configs` calls `ConfigCoordinator` on the Node host, so it writes no start time and no run status — to see the summary on the sheet, tick the sync endpoint's checkbox instead. On the command line the summary rides back with the four file sources (`ConfigRegeneration.untypedColumnsSummary`) and the script prints it, because a command line has no cell to write into and the only signal the sync produces would otherwise be lost; the per-sheet breakdown still goes to the log. **The agent must report that count**, per the standing permission in [`docs/how-it-runs.md`](../how-it-runs.md).

## The generated entry never says which step decided it

**The generated entry itself never says which step decided it.** A declared `CURRENCY` column type and a `CURRENCY` number format under a blank top cell both emit `valueName: "number"`, so a wrong value name in `columnConfigs.ts` doesn't tell you whether to change a declaration or add one. That summary is the only signal the app gives; from outside it, read the live declared types directly (see [`docs/how-it-runs.md`](../how-it-runs.md) "The `gsheets` MCP tools").
